scope: The existing Saturday Spin P0 release plus the Not Done Yet application workflow, including the five-question initial application with preferred start timing, deliberate staged post-submission review, supported-mobile haptics, approved next-step presentation, explanatory Beehiiv email, personal actions, delivery APIs, admin follow-up views, analytics privacy controls and scheduled retries.

sections.readerQuestion: Can readers rely on the corrected newsletter reach and stable Core Training Guide delivery introduced on main?
sections.usefulAnswer: The inherited main revision retains the corrected 23,000-reader proof, attribution handling and verified PDF route.
sections.evidence: Main already carried exact-revision publication evidence for these surfaces before the Not Done Yet branch was reconciled.
sections.editorialDecision: Preserve the reviewed main-branch work without reopening or weakening its claims.

sections.location: /apply form, confirmation, /apply/next review transition and after-application FAQ
sections.readerQuestion: What happens when I submit my coaching application?
sections.usefulAnswer: The initial form asks five quick questions, including whether the rider wants to start right now, in the coming weeks or on a specific future date. With the feature enabled, a saved Not Done Yet application then moves through four review messages over eight seconds before confirming approval and offering the join and Sarah paths; compatible coarse-pointer mobile browsers receive subtle haptic cues and Inner Circle retains its existing process.
sections.evidence: Anthony requested the immediate two-option flow on 8 September 2026, then approved the longer staged review, final copy and mobile haptics on 9 September 2026. On 9 September 2026 he also requested the new start-timing question and supplied its three answer choices. The server flag gates the follow-up workflow and visible form copy.
sections.editorialDecision: Require start timing for Not Done Yet applications, reveal a date selector only for the specific-date choice, reject past dates, preserve Inner Circle's existing process, present the deterministic result after a deliberate eight-second transition, avoid implying a separate human decision, and treat vibration as a progressive enhancement only where the browser supports it.

sections.location: /apply/next approval, join, onboarding and questions sections
sections.readerQuestion: How do I join, or ask about the coaching before paying?
sections.usefulAnswer: Approved applicants can start a seven-day free trial in Skool with no charge until it ends, see the stated monthly price, learn that the team will arrange onboarding once they are inside, or ask Sarah to hold their place, arrange a later start or answer questions.
sections.evidence: The live Skool plan was checked at seven days free followed by $195 USD per month plus applicable taxes. Anthony supplied and approved the signup, onboarding and Sarah hold-or-question instructions.
sections.editorialDecision: Keep the two actions and two numbered steps explicit; describe availability without a countdown, quantity or unsupported scarcity claim.

sections.location: Application API, database outbox, live Beehiiv automation, cron and Anthony notification sender
sections.readerQuestion: Will applications and questions survive a delivery problem?
sections.usefulAnswer: The application and email job commit together; questions save before notification; known failures retry within bounds while uncertain enrollments stop for inspection.
sections.evidence: Focused workflow tests cover deduplication, opt-outs, marker ordering, accepted-journey confirmation, saved questions, Anthony routing and retry boundaries; the production table, draft transactions, live provider configuration and published Beehiiv email were also verified.
sections.editorialDecision: Use precise delivery states, preserve opt-outs and payment state, and never equate checkout interest with payment.

sections.readerQuestion: Can staff see who needs a reply without exposing a personal action token?
sections.usefulAnswer: Authenticated staff can see each rider's preferred start timing in the application detail and Sarah Review queue alongside delivery and question status, while analytics and referrer leakage are suppressed on the personal next-step page.
sections.evidence: The implementation stores the start choice and optional date on the application record, exposes them through existing authenticated admin views, assigns question records to Sarah, alerts Anthony, and keeps personal tokens in URL fragments and POST bodies rather than query strings.
sections.editorialDecision: Expose useful operational states only to staff and scope analytics suppression to the personal action surface.

claimsAndSources: The workflow and inbox routing come from Anthony's 8 September 2026 instructions; the staged review, mobile haptics, signup, onboarding and Sarah hold-or-question language were supplied and approved by Anthony on 9 September 2026. Anthony also supplied the new start-timing question and its Right now, Coming weeks and Specific date choices on 9 September 2026. The seven-day trial and $195 USD monthly price were checked on the live Skool plan; Sarah's direct address and ownership are confirmed in repository configuration. Existing main-branch audience and PDF claims remain unchanged.
examplesAndReasoning: The suitability result is determined by the existing goal, time and injury/comeback routing rule before this page loads. The four-message transition presents that completed application review; it is not described as a medical or human assessment. No training prescription or member result is invented.
voiceAndCuts: The approved state and email use the requested congratulatory tone, two numbered setup steps and a calm Sarah alternative. The transition gives each of the four review messages two seconds, creating a deliberate pause without a countdown, queue-position or limited-place claim.
desktopReview: The exact source was rendered at 1432 by 900 CSS pixels for the five-step application, staged review and approved personal next-step page. The new question displayed all three timing choices, Specific date revealed a future-date selector, the selected date survived back navigation, and the page had no horizontal overflow. The prior four-message and published Beehiiv email reviews remain applicable.
mobileReview: The exact source was rendered in a 390 by 844 CSS pixel browser viewport for the five-step application and personal next-step surface. The timing choices stacked into usable full-width buttons, Coming weeks advanced to the final details step, and the page had no horizontal overflow. The prior staged-review and Beehiiv mobile email reviews remain applicable.
productAndOfferAccuracy: The live Skool offer showed a seven-day free trial followed by $195 USD per month plus applicable taxes. The dedicated Beehiiv automation is live with the approved two-step instructions, personalised destinations and a neutral preview line; the publication reply-to remains Anthony. Website questions persist in Sarah Review and send Anthony an operational alert.
